conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 10 High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 10 High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps

summaryBox.title: NEST Exam Traps
summaryBox.takeaway: Cl has more negative Δ_eg H than F; Δ_eg H₂ is always endothermic; r(Ga) < r(Al); Zr ≈ Hf; Pb²⁺ is more stable than Pb⁴⁺.

conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Electron Gain Enthalpy of Halogens**: $\text{Cl} (-349\text{ kJ/mol})$ has a MORE negative $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$ than $\text{F} (-328\text{ kJ/mol})$. Fluorine has highest electronegativity, NOT electron gain enthalpy.
2. **Group 16 Electron Gain Enthalpy**: Oxygen has the LEAST negative $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$ in Group 16 ($\text{S} > \text{Se} > \text{Te} > \text{Po} > \text{O}$).
3. **Second Electron Gain Enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2$)**: ALWAYS ENDOTHERMIC ($\Delta > 0$) for all elements without exception ($\text{O}^- + e^- \rightarrow \text{O}^{2-}$ is $+780\text{ kJ/mol}$).
4. **Aqueous Alkali Mobility**: $\text{Li}^+(\text{aq})$ moves SLOWEST due to its massive hydrated shell; $\text{Cs}^+(\text{aq})$ moves fastest.
5. **Group 13 Radii**: $r(\text{Ga}) < r(\text{Al})$ ($1.35\text{ \AA}$ vs $1.43\text{ \AA}$) due to poor shielding of $10\ 3d$-electrons (Scandide contraction).
6. **Octet Expansion Restriction**: $\text{NCl}_5$ is impossible because Nitrogen belongs to Period 2 and lacks vacant $d$-orbitals.
7. **Lanthanide Radii Match**: $4d$ and $5d$ transition elements have almost identical radii ($r(\text{Zr}) \approx r(\text{Hf}) = 1.59\text{ \AA}$) due to $4f^{14}$ Lanthanide contraction.
8. **First Ionization Enthalpy of Nitrogen vs Oxygen**: $\text{IE}_1(\text{N}) > \text{IE}_1(\text{O})$ due to stable half-filled $2p^3$ subshell.
9. **Slater Rules Shielding**: For $4s$, $3d$ electrons act as $(n-1)$ shell contributing $0.85$ each; for $3d$, other $3d$ contribute $0.35$.
10. **Inert Pair Effect & Lead Stability**: $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ is much more stable than $\text{Pb}^{4+}$; $\text{PbO}_2$ is a powerful oxidizing agent.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.2 Master Chemistry Glossary (36 Terms)
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.2 Master Chemistry Glossary (36 Terms)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Actinide Contraction**: Steady decrease in radii across 5f actinides due to poor 5f shielding.
• **Allred-Rochow Scale**: Electronegativity based on electrostatic force: $\chi = 0.359 (Z_{\text{eff}}/r^2) + 0.744$.
• **Amphoteric Oxide**: Oxide reacting with both acids and bases ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, \text{BeO}, \text{ZnO}, \text{PbO}, \text{SnO}_2$).
• **Covalent Radius ($r_{\text{cov}}$)**: Half internuclear distance between single-bonded identical atoms.
• **Diagonal Relationship**: Chemical similarity between Period 2 ($\text{Li, Be, B}$) and Period 3 ($\text{Mg, Al, Si}$) diagonal pairs.
• **Effective Nuclear Charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$)**: Net positive charge experienced by electron: $Z_{\text{eff}} = Z - \sigma$.
• **Electron Gain Enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$)**: Enthalpy change on electron addition to neutral isolated gaseous atom.
• **Electronegativity ($\chi$)**: Tendency of a bonded atom to attract shared electron pairs.
• **Hydration Enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H$)**: Exothermic energy released on ion hydration ($\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H \propto z^2/r$).
• **Inert Pair Effect**: Reluctance of outer $ns^2$ valence electrons to bond in heavy $p$-block ($\text{Tl, Pb, Bi}$).
• **Ionization Enthalpy ($\Delta_i H$)**: Minimum energy to remove most loosely bound electron from isolated neutral gaseous atom.
• **Isoelectronic Series**: Species possessing identical total electron counts ($r \propto 1/Z$).
• **Lanthanide Contraction**: Steady radius decrease across 4f series causing $4d \approx 5d$ radii.
• **Moseley's Law**: Linear relation $\sqrt{\nu} = a(Z-b)$ proving $Z$ is fundamental.
• **Mulliken Scale**: Electronegativity defined as average of IE and EA: $\chi_M = (\text{IE}+\text{EA})/2$.
• **Pauling Scale**: Electronegativity based on bond dissociation energies: $\chi_A - \chi_B = 0.102\sqrt{\Delta}$.
• **Scandide Contraction**: Radius reduction in post-$3d$ elements ($r(\text{Ga}) < r(\text{Al})$).
• **Slater's Rules**: Semi-empirical rules calculating screening constant $\sigma$.
• **Van der Waals Radius ($r_{\text{vdw}}$)**: Half distance between non-bonded adjacent atoms in solid state ($r_{\text{vdw}} > r_{\text{met}} > r_{\text{cov}}$).

quickRevision: Cl has highest negative Δ_eg H; F has highest Electronegativity.
Δ_eg H₂ is always positive (+780 kJ/mol for Oxygen).
r(Ga) < r(Al) due to Scandide contraction.
r(Zr) ≈ r(Hf) due to Lanthanide contraction.
Pb²⁺ > Pb⁴⁺ stability due to Inert pair effect.
